attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, rebutting a booster quip.

semantics.note: An unqualified 'No it won't', backed by a writeup about foundation models, makes this a forecast with no deadline. The normalised wording keeps the scope.

contract.note: Reading it as independent, substantive research, not mere assistance, fits his 'insufficient' framing. The autonomy and validation thresholds are the evaluator's, so the result depends on that interpretation.

evidence.note: Nature paper on an end-to-end AI Scientist. Its manuscript only passed a first-round workshop review, which is not independent validation of a substantive scientific result under the contract.
Independent preprint finds Kosmos produced one well-supported finding plus failures. It is limited and does not establish model-led, independently validated research meeting the autonomy criteria.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline, so a period without a qualifying example cannot support it. The evidence shows growing model-led research, but nothing in the packet meets the contract's bar of independently validated, substantively autonomous research. The strongest candidate could not be read. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: An observation about the state of evidence when he published. The wording keeps 'no proof' and the young-people scope.

contract.note: Reading 'proof' as credible causal identification, not mere correlation or suggestion, is an ordinary and fair plain reading. Limiting it to research available by publication is appropriate.

evidence.note: EIG analysis dated before the post finds young-worker unemployment rising whether workers were AI-exposed or not, so no causal effect was shown.
The Oxford economist gives suggestive evidence alongside other explanations, such as hiring normalisation. That is not a causal design.

reviews.rationale: Research available by publication shows young people's job difficulties but no established causal link to AI. EIG found similar trends for exposed and unexposed young workers. The Oxford view was suggestive and allowed other causes. A search cannot rule out every study, but the packet supports the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'Basically the same' is rendered faithfully as essentially the same. Claude and Grok are the named comparators.

contract.note: Practical substitutability at comparable consumer tiers is a fair ordinary reading, given the context about products, cost and functions. The tolerance for differences is unstated.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own GPT-5 launch disclosure lists ChatGPT's tasks. It does not compare the three products.
Anthropic's own disclosure shows Claude has overlapping research and coding functions. It does not compare with the others.
xAI's own disclosure shows Grok's tool use and X search integration. It shows overlap and one distinctive feature, not whether the products are equivalent.

reviews.rationale: The packet holds only the vendors' own descriptions. They show overlapping functions but no independent, dated comparison of task performance, features, limits or prices. Substitutability can be neither confirmed nor refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'I don't think so' states belief with uncertainty, and the study he cites only 'suggested' a slowdown. The normalised text keeps 'in his view' but treats the claim as scoreable, dropping the hedge.

contract.note: The contract scores hedged language on a plain reading despite flagging the hedge, which the policy forbids. The February–June 2025 period and the net completion-time metric are evaluator inventions.

evidence.note: METR randomised trial in the period found a 19% slowdown, but only for 16 experienced developers on familiar repositories. It cannot settle a hedged claim.
METR says its sample does not represent most development work.
Google randomised trial found a speedup of about 21%, but in summer 2024, outside the chosen period.

reviews.rationale: 'I don't think so' expresses hedged belief, like 'I suspect', so under the policy it is not scored. The evidence is also mixed and narrow: one slowdown in a limited sample, plus an out-of-period speedup.
